linkedin.hook: You can tell which AI agents are going to fail in production by asking one question: how do you measure when this agent gets worse?
linkedin.body:
Most teams answer some version of "we don't." That's how an AI initiative becomes the AI thing that keeps embarrassing you.

We hard-code a different rule into every VioX OS deployment: no agent ships without an eval suite. Day zero. Before the agent talks to a real user.

Three reasons it has to be up front:

· Models drift. The Claude Sonnet you tested last month isn't the same weights today.
· Prompts decay. Every "improvement" has a 1-in-3 chance of breaking three other cases.
· Tools change. APIs add fields. Your agent silently hallucinates around it.

The four-tier suite every VioX OS agent ships with:

Tier 1 — Smoke (~20 cases, runs every commit)
Tier 2 — Capability (~80-150 cases, runs nightly)
Tier 3 — Adversarial (~30 cases — prompt injections, jailbreaks)
Tier 4 — Regression (every production failure becomes a permanent test)

The rule that matters: a falling score is a fact, not a vibe.

If you can't answer "what's the eval score this week?" — pick 20 representative customer interactions, write a rubric, score them, run weekly. That's it. 20 scored cases is dramatically better than what most teams running production agents have today.

Ask the team "how do you measure when this agent gets worse?"
Most answers: "we don't." That's how an AI project becomes the AI thing that keeps embarrassing you.
We hard-code a different rule into every VioX OS deployment: no agent ships without an eval suite. Day zero.

Three reasons it has to be up front:
· Models drift
· Prompts decay
· Tools change

Without evals you find out from a customer.

The 4-tier suite every VioX OS agent ships with:

T1 — Smoke (every commit)
T2 — Capability (nightly)
T3 — Adversarial (jailbreaks, injections)
T4 — Regression (every production failure becomes permanent test)

Rule that matters: a falling score is a fact, not a vibe. When the Closer's email-quality drops 7.4→6.8 in a week, we look at which regression cases failed. We don't argue about whether it "feels worse."

Cant' answer "what's the eval score this week?" — 20 cases, write a rubric, score weekly. Better than 95% of teams running prod agents today.
